assumptions.assumption: _rect_clear correctly computes distance to robot's body rectangle
assumptions.why: _rect_clear uses max((x_max - rx), (rx - x_min)) which overestimates distance when point is outside rectangle (e.g., rx=0.36 > x_max=0.36 gives 0.0 but ry=-0.55 < y_min=-0.36 gives 0.19, yet reported distances are much larger)

assumptions.assumption: MTC calculation accurately reflects time to collision
assumptions.why: Overestimated clr leads to inflated MTC (e.g., 0.2m distance reported as 1.4m), delaying stop commands and causing collisions or prolonged stalls

approach_families.result: partial success but collisions persisted due to core distance calculation flaw

approach_families.result: failed when clr error dominated MTC accuracy

candidates.idea: Fix _rect_clear to compute correct Euclidean distance to body rectangle
candidates.for: directly addresses clr overestimation causing delayed collision response
candidates.risk: requires precise geometric calculation; may introduce edge-case errors

candidates.idea: Replace _rect_clear with direct body bound checks using min/max
candidates.for: simpler and more accurate distance calculation
candidates.risk: may miss points near diagonal edges of body rectangle

candidates.idea: Use 3D lidar points with height filtering for collision detection
candidates.risk: computationally heavier; 2D lidar already covers floor obstacles

diagnosis.chosen: Fix _rect_clear to correctly compute minimum distance to robot body rectangle
diagnosis.direction: Rewrite _rect_clear to compute horizontal distance as max(0, rx - x_max, x_min - rx) and vertical as max(0, ry - y_max, y_min - ry), then clr = sqrt(ddx² + ddy²). This ensures accurate proximity detection to body edges.
